# Module 6: Validation and Testing (Default Behavior)

## 📚 Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, you will be able to:

- Understand default validation and test generation behavior in v1.0.0+
- Use `--no-validate` and `--no-test` flags when needed
- Work with generated validation decorators and test scaffolds

---

## 6.1 Default behavior (v1.0.0+)

**✅ Tests are generated by default**  
**✅ Validation decorators are added by default**

```bash
# This command generates everything with tests and validation
eqxjs-swagger-codegen generate -i ./swagger.json -o ./generated
```

This is a significant change from earlier versions where you had to opt-in with `--with-test` and `--with-validate`.

---

## 6.2 Generated validation decorators

The generator automatically adds class-validator decorators to DTOs based on schema metadata:

**Common decorators:**

- `@IsString()`, `@IsNumber()`, `@IsInt()`, `@IsBoolean()`, `@IsDate()` - basic types
- `@IsEmail()` - email format validation
- `@IsUUID()` - UUID format validation
- `@IsUrl()` - URL format validation
- `@IsEnum()` - enum value validation
- `@IsArray()` with `@IsString({ each: true })` - array validation
- `@ValidateNested()` with `@Type()` - nested object validation
- `@Min()`, `@Max()` - number constraints
- `@MinLength()`, `@MaxLength()` - string length constraints
- `@Matches()` - regex pattern validation

**Example generated DTO:**

```typescript
import { ApiProperty } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { IsString, IsEmail, IsInt, Min } from 'class-validator';

export class CreateUserDto {
  @IsString()
  @IsEmail()
  @ApiProperty({ description: 'User email', type: String })
  email!: string;

  @IsInt()
  @Min(18)
  @ApiProperty({ description: 'User age', type: Number })
  age!: number;
}
```

---

## 6.3 Generated test files

Test files are automatically created in a `tests/` directory with the same structure as your generated code:

**Example structure:**

```
generated/
├── dtos/
│   ├── user.dto.ts
│   └── create-user-dto.dto.ts
├── users/
│   ├── users.service.ts
│   ├── users.controller.ts
│   └── users.module.ts
└── tests/
    ├── dtos/
    │   ├── user.dto.spec.ts
    │   └── create-user-dto.dto.spec.ts
    └── users/
        ├── users.controller.spec.ts
        └── users.service.spec.ts
```

**Test scaffolds include:**

- DTO instantiation tests
- Controller endpoint tests with mocked services
- Service method tests with basic assertions

---

## 6.4 Skipping validation or tests

Use negative flags to skip generation when needed:

```bash
# Skip validation decorators (faster generation, lighter DTOs)
eqxjs-swagger-codegen generate -i ./swagger.json -o ./generated --no-validate

# Skip test file generation (rapid prototyping)
eqxjs-swagger-codegen generate -i ./swagger.json -o ./generated --no-test

# Skip both (minimal output, plain DTOs)
eqxjs-swagger-codegen generate -i ./swagger.json -o ./generated --no-test --no-validate
```

---

## 6.5 Practical guidance

**Validation best practices:**

- Keep validation in the DTO layer for contract consistency
- Use ValidationPipe in your NestJS app to enforce validation automatically
- Add custom validators when business rules go beyond schema metadata

**Testing best practices:**

- Treat generated tests as scaffolds, not complete test suites
- Extend generated tests with edge cases and integration scenarios
- Run lint/build/test in CI after every regeneration to catch breaking changes

---

## 6.6 Example: Validation in action

**Setup ValidationPipe in `main.ts`:**

```typescript
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
  
  // Enable validation globally
  app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({
    whitelist: true,
    forbidNonWhitelisted: true,
    transform: true,
  }));
  
  await app.listen(3000);
}
bootstrap();
```

Now all generated DTOs with validation decorators will be automatically validated on incoming requests.

---

## ✅ Summary

- **v1.0.0+ generates tests and validation by default** - no flags needed
- Use `--no-validate` or `--no-test` to skip when needed
- Generated validation decorators provide runtime contract enforcement
- Generated tests accelerate initial test coverage setup
